response.thesis: In Memento, memory functions as an unreliable and fragmented system that shapes Leonard's identity and actions, revealing how his short-term memory loss forces him to depend on external aids and creates a subjective, unstable reality that challenges traditional narrative and perception

evidence_cards.label: Scene
evidence_cards.title: Leonard Explains His Condition to Burt in the Motel Office
evidence_cards.body: In this scene, Leonard openly describes his rare short-term memory loss condition to Burt, explaining that he cannot form new memories and forgets conversations quickly. The dialogue reveals Leonard's reliance on external tools like Polaroid photos and notes to maintain continuity in his life. Burt's confused and incredulous reactions highlight how Leonard's memory impairment isolates him socially and complicates his interactions. This scene directly shows Leonard's fragmented memory and how it shapes his reality, emphasizing this lens of memory's unreliability and its impact on identity

evidence_cards.label: Character
evidence_cards.title: Leonard's Use of Polaroid Photos and Notes
evidence_cards.body: Leonard's behavior of taking Polaroid photos, writing notes, and tattooing key facts on his body embodies his struggle with memory loss. These external aids compensate for his inability to remember new information, showing his dependence on physical reminders to construct a coherent sense of self and purpose. His meticulous system reflects his attempt to impose order on his fragmented experience, and reveals how memory is mediated and subjective, raising questions about the authenticity of his knowledge and motivations

evidence_cards.label: Pattern
evidence_cards.title: Nonlinear Narrative Structure and Repeated Scenes
evidence_cards.body: The film's editing and storytelling use a nonlinear, backward sequence interspersed with black-and-white forward-moving scenes, reflecting Leonard's disoriented memory state. Repetitions of scenes with slight variations highlight the instability of memory and perception. This pattern of fragmented chronology forces viewers to experience the story as Leonard does, emphasizing how memory loss distorts reality and complicates the search for truth. The editing style itself becomes a motif reinforcing this lens of memory's unreliability

evidence_cards.label: Counterreading
evidence_cards.title: Teddy’s Skepticism About Leonard’s Memory and Notes
evidence_cards.body: Teddy challenges Leonard’s reliance on his notes and memories, warning that they might be flawed or manipulated. This skepticism complicates the thesis by introducing doubt about Leonard’s constructed reality and motivations, showing that memory loss fragments experience and opens space for manipulation and self-delusion, which destabilizes the viewer’s trust in Leonard’s perspective

evidence_cards.label: Character

evidence_cards.label: Character
